text.en: At a science centre Meena sees a curved mirror that makes her look tall and thin, and another that makes her look short and wide. How can mirrors change how we look?

Light travels in straight lines, and when it falls on a smooth surface it bounces back, which is called reflection.
The laws of reflection: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and both rays and the normal lie in one plane.
A plane mirror forms an upright image of the same size, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, and it is laterally inverted.
A concave mirror curves inward like the inside of a spoon and can make magnified images when the object is close.
A convex mirror curves outward and always forms smaller, upright images with a wide view, so it is used as a rear-view mirror.
Lenses bend light by refraction, which is the change of direction of light when it passes from one medium to another.
A convex lens is thick in the middle and converges light, so it is used as a magnifying glass and in cameras.
A concave lens is thin in the middle and spreads light out, and it is used to correct short-sightedness.
Spoons, torches, car headlights and telescopes use curved mirrors and lenses.
White light splits into seven colours VIBGYOR, which we see in a rainbow, because each colour bends by a different amount.

problem.en: A ray hits a plane mirror at 30° to the normal. What is the angle of reflection?

text.en: Angle of reflection equals angle of incidence.
So the angle of reflection is 30°.

prompt.en: Why is a convex mirror used as a rear-view mirror?

requiredIdeas.en: It gives a wide field of view.

points.en: Reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
Concave and convex mirrors and lenses form different images.
Refraction bends light; white light splits into VIBGYOR.
